pageContent.markdown:
Lee Broom flagship showroom, Rivington Street, Shoreditch

# Lee Broom x Calico Wallpaper: 'Overture' at the Lee Broom Shoreditch showroom

Lee Broom's first wallpaper, a trompe-l'oeil theatre curtain, brought to the UK for London Design Festival 2025, measured for a bespoke panel layout and hung.

![Overture drapery wallpaper beside a chandelier.](https://www.mrwallcover.com/media/img/r/lee-broom-08-800.webp)

## At a glance

Client, materials & project facts

**Client**
: Calico Wallpaper (Brooklyn, New York), for Lee Broom

**Designer**
: Lee Broom

**Main contractor**
: –Not recorded

**Maker and paper**
: Calico Wallpaper x Lee Broom – Overture (installed design: Matinee)

**Area or rooms**
: –Not recorded

**Scope**
: Survey, wall preparation and installation of the Overture mural; wallpapering of theatrical flats for Calico's LDF dinner

**Year**
: 2025

**Delivered in partnership with [Calico Wallpaper](https://calicowallpaper.com/).**

**In the press:** [Lee Broom, “Lee Broom x Calico Wallpaper present Overture”](https://leebroom.com/collaboration/lee-broom-x-calico-wallpaper-present-overture/) · [Lee Broom, *Trio of Design*, LDF 2025](https://leebroom.com/exhibition/london-design-festival-2025trio-of-designthree-presentations-at-the-lee-broom-shoreditch-showroom/) · [ICON Magazine](https://www.iconeye.com/design/lee-broom-invites-visitors-into-a-unique-showcase-of-his-ground-breaking-work-from-the-past-year) · [CC Magazine](https://ccmagazine.es/en/lee-broom-trio-of-design-london-design-festival-2025/)

## At a glance

- **In partnership with:** Calico Wallpaper, Brooklyn, with Lee Broom
- **Event:** London Design Festival 2025, *Trio of Design*, Lee Broom’s Shoreditch flagship, 16–21 September 2025
- **Collection:** Overture, Lee Broom’s first-ever wallpaper (installed design: Matinee)
- **Our work:**
  - survey and measurements for Calico’s layout
  - wall preparation
  - installation of the mural across a side wall and a back wall with a concealed door
  - wallpapered theatrical flats for Calico’s LDF dinner
- **Dates:** surveyed July 2025; installed 9 September 2025

## The collection

Overture grew out of Lee Broom’s childhood as a child actor and his fascination with theatre drapery: “the huge draped curtains with painted backdrops” and sets that played tricks with perspective. The wallpaper is a trompe-l’oeil curtain that turns a flat wall into a stage. First shown in New York, it was “reimagined for the London audience” in one of three rooms of Lee Broom’s Rivington Street showroom.

## Our approach

- **Measured for a bespoke layout.** We surveyed the room in July 2025 and supplied the dimensions from which Calico drew the panel layout. Overture is made to measure, so the folds of the curtain fall exactly where the room needs them.
- **Wall preparation.** The showroom walls were filled and sanded smooth. A drapery illusion only works if no real-world bump or ripple breaks the painted folds.
- **Large-format panels, double cut.** Calico’s fibre panels, about 68 cm wide, are hung with a bleed and double cut on the wall. That gives invisible seams through the soft gradients of the folds.
- **Hiding the door.** On the back wall the curtain runs straight across a flush door. The pattern is carried over it so that the door disappears into the drape.

## The dinner flats

For Calico’s London Design Festival dinner the same September, we also papered freestanding theatrical flats in a set builder’s workshop on 15 September 2025, ready to be moved into the dining venue.

## Outcome

From 16 to 21 September 2025, visitors to Shoreditch Design Triangle walked into a room that appeared to be draped in theatre curtains.

## Photographs

![Detail of an Overture flat ready for Calico's London Design Festival dinner.](https://www.mrwallcover.com/media/img/r/lee-broom-11-800.webp)

![Overture panels on the side wall of the showroom.](https://www.mrwallcover.com/media/img/r/lee-broom-04-800.webp)

![Overture drapery wallpaper hung across the room at Lee Broom's Shoreditch showroom, before the room was dressed.](https://www.mrwallcover.com/media/img/r/lee-broom-03-800.webp)

![Calico Wallpaper Overture trompe-l'oeil curtain carried across a concealed door at Lee Broom's Shoreditch showroom.](https://www.mrwallcover.com/media/img/r/lee-broom-01-800.webp)

![A full Overture drop hung, before trimming at the skirting.](https://www.mrwallcover.com/media/img/r/lee-broom-07-800.webp)

![Overture panels aligned at the top of the wall during installation.](https://www.mrwallcover.com/media/img/r/lee-broom-05-800.webp)

![Setting out an Overture panel against a laser line.](https://www.mrwallcover.com/media/img/r/lee-broom-06-800.webp)

![A theatrical flat papered in Overture on the workshop bench.](https://www.mrwallcover.com/media/img/r/lee-broom-09-800.webp)

![A papered Overture flat standing in the set builder's workshop.](https://www.mrwallcover.com/media/img/r/lee-broom-10-800.webp)

How the commission ran

## The same standards, on every commission.

Whether the client is a hotel group, a designer or a household, the job runs the same way. These are the parts a photograph never shows.

01

### Survey and scope, room by room

We measure the wall that will actually be hung, allow for the repeat and the wastage, and write a scope of works room by room before anyone orders paper.

02

### Preparation decides the finish

Walls are filled, made good and primed until they are true. If a wall is not ready for the material specified, we say so before the last drop is ordered.

03

### Protection and containment

Floors, furniture and finished joinery are protected as part of the hang. Work is contained and the place is left tidy each evening. In a home we are visitors; in a hotel we work around the house.

04

### Batch and shade control

Deliveries are checked against the measure, and batches and shading are managed so that a corridor of rooms reads as one surface.

05

### Set out from the room's focal points

Pattern is set out from chimneypieces, doorcases and bed walls, so the design meets the cornice and the joinery with composure.

06

### One team, then the return visit

The people who start are the people who finish. Four to six weeks after completion we come back to look at every seam and edge, and the workmanship is guaranteed for twelve months.

[See the finish up close: seams, internal corners, edges and joins from our own installations](https://www.mrwallcover.com/details/)

By [Dorin Burcus](https://www.mrwallcover.com/about/#dorin), founder · Last updated 10 October 2026
